key_cases.case_name: In re Welfare of the Child of B.J.-M.
key_cases.holding: Exercising its supervisory power over the Rules of Juvenile Protection Procedure, the court held that a parent's rights cannot be terminated unless the termination petition names that parent as a party to the proceeding.
key_cases.relevance: It fixes the minimum content of the petition that opens a Minnesota juvenile-protection case against a given parent.
key_cases.quote: a parent's parental rights cannot be terminated in the absence of a petition naming the parent as a party to the proceedings

key_cases.case_name: In re Welfare of Child of M.K.
key_cases.holding: The court held that parents were entitled to withdraw CHIPS admissions that the county obtained by threatening to withhold needed services, because accepting admissions extracted that way was a manifest injustice.
key_cases.relevance: It addresses directly the decision to file a CHIPS petition and take admissions on it.
key_cases.quote: we conclude that a threat to act in a manner that is not in a child's best interests constitutes a manifest injustice

key_cases.case_name: In re Welfare of the Children of L.K.
key_cases.holding: The court held that former foster parents were properly denied permissive intervention and that their third-party custody petition was properly dismissed, so they are not parties to the children's CHIPS case, and it vacated the court of appeals' constitutional ruling.
key_cases.relevance: It defines who is and is not a party once a CHIPS case is opened, and therefore who may litigate the child's placement.
key_cases.quote: We hold that the district court did not err in denying appellants' petition for permissive intervention and in dismissing their third-party custody petition.

key_cases.case_name: In re Welfare of the Children of Coats
key_cases.holding: Reversing the court of appeals and reinstating the district court's default judgment, the court held that a mother who signed a notice warning that default could be entered, failed to appear at the pretrial hearing, and showed neither a reasonable defense on the merits nor a reasonable excuse was not entitled to Rule 60.02 relief, and that the resulting termination was not void for lack of due process.
key_cases.relevance: It fixes what can follow the filing of a petition: a parent served with a notice warning of default who does not personally appear may have the petition granted on the merits at the pretrial hearing, without a trial and after counsel is allowed to withdraw.
key_cases.quote: Accordingly, we hold that the default judgment is not void for lack of due process.

state_agency.name: Minnesota Department of Children, Youth, and Families
state_agency.hotline: No statewide hotline. Call the county or Tribal child protection agency where the child lives — the directory link is on dcyf.mn.gov/individuals-and-families/report-abuse

timeline_requirements.deadline: Safety assessment completed at the face-to-face contact with the child and the child's primary caregiver, which must be sufficient to ensure the immediate safety of the child
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Receipt of a screened in report
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in Minn. Stat. § 260E.20; subd. 2(a) requires the face-to-face contact to be sufficient to complete a safety assessment and ensure the immediate safety of the child.

Not specified by statute; Minn. Stat. § 260E.24, subd. 3 requires the two determinations at the conclusion of the investigation and subd. 5 requires written notice within ten working days of that conclusion.

timeline_requirements.starts_from: Receipt of notice of the investigating agency's final determination regarding maltreatment
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in Minn. Stat. § 260E.33; subd. 2 requires the written request within 15 calendar days after receipt of notice of the final determination, subd. 3 allows a fair hearing only after the agency denies the reconsideration request or fails to act on it within 15 working days, and subd. 1 provides no reconsideration after a family assessment or noncaregiver human trafficking assessment because no maltreatment determination is made.
